n3bfc2a7cad5.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no clear dates)
n3bfc2a7cad5.s: The earliest literary reference to the Andhras occurs in the:
n3bfc2a7cad5.x: The Aitareya Brahmana gives the earliest literary reference to the Andhras, in the story of Sunahshepa and Vishwamitra's disowned sons.

nap-history-1-29.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Kalamalla inscription, the first Telugu inscription
2. Magallu inscription, the first to mention the Kakatiyas
3. First Muslim invasion of Warangal, sent by Alauddin Khilji
nap-history-1-29.x: The first Telugu inscription (Kalamalla) predates the first mention of the Kakatiyas (Magallu), and the Kakatiyas were attacked by Alauddin Khilji's forces only in 1303.

n6e5050b8118.s: Which of the following is regarded as the most reliable source for ancient Indian history?
n6e5050b8118.x: Inscriptions are regarded as the most reliable source; foreign accounts only supplement them where Indian texts are silent.

n9292463d004.s: The Arikamedu excavation of 1945 was conducted by:
n9292463d004.x: Mortimer Wheeler excavated Arikamedu in 1945; Marshall worked at Mohenjodaro, Rea at Bhattiprolu and Longhurst at Nagarjunakonda.

n170341d4802.s: Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions have been found at all of the following EXCEPT:
n170341d4802.x: Kandahar has Ashokan inscriptions in Greek and Aramaic, not Tamil-Brahmi; Mangulam is in the Pandya region and Berenike and Quseir al-Qadim are in Egypt.

n8f9de110ffb.s: The Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra edicts of Ashoka are written in which script?
n8f9de110ffb.x: Kharosthi, a right-to-left script of north-western India, is used in the Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra edicts.

n59431648c1a.s: Which inscription contains the first edict naming Ashoka as "Asoka"?
n59431648c1a.x: The Maski inscription is the first edict to name Ashoka as Asoka; it also uses the term Gulmika.

n560144dd592.s: The Milindapanho records a dialogue between Menander and:
n560144dd592.x: The Milindapanho records the dialogue between the Indo-Greek king Menander and the monk Nagasena.

nindian-history-1-59.s: The Hathigumpha inscription shows that Kharavela followed which religion?
nindian-history-1-59.x: The Hathigumpha inscription opens with a salute to the Jinas, showing Kharavela's Jainism.

nindian-history-30-15.x: Annamacharya, the earliest known Telugu song-composer, is called Padakavita Pitamaha.

nap-history-14-4.x: Karpanamulu were Satavahana copper coins; nishkam, tankam and varaha were Kakatiya gold coins.

nindian-history-1-95.s: Who repaired the Sudarshana lake without using forced labour?
nindian-history-1-95.x: Rudradaman I's Junagadh inscription at Girnar records that he repaired the Sudarshana lake without forced labour.

nindian-history-54-18.s: Which traveller wrote on Hindu religion, the Puranas, Sanskrit and Yoga?
nindian-history-54-18.x: Al-Biruni wrote on Hindu learning; I-Tsing wrote on Buddhist relics and Fa-Hien on Buddhist pilgrimage.

nd8554cf6621.x: The Samarangana Sutradhara is King Bhoja's work; Somadeva Suri wrote Nitivakyamrita and Vatsabhatti composed the Dashpur inscription.

nc3914a64dc8.s: The Dipavamsa and Mahavamsa are Pali chronicles of:
nc3914a64dc8.x: The Dipavamsa and Mahavamsa are Sri Lankan Pali chronicles that illuminate Mauryan history and Buddhism.

nee7ec6395d2.s: The Nasik Prashasti praising Gautamiputra Satakarni was composed by:
nee7ec6395d2.x: Gautami Balashri, mother of Gautamiputra Satakarni, composed the Nasik Prashasti hailing him as destroyer of the Shakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas.

n2bca626a6bb.s: According to the Puranas, the last Satavahana ruler was:
n2bca626a6bb.x: The Puranas name Pulomavi III as the last Satavahana, not Gautamiputra Satakarni.

nindian-history-97-19.x: Rajasekhara wrote the Kavyamimamsa; Kalidasa was the great Sanskrit poet of the Gupta age.

nindian-history-54-12.s: Which foreign writer described Indian society in terms of Brahmins and Shramanas?
nindian-history-54-12.x: Megasthenes wrote of Brahmins and Shramanas; Fa-Hien, Hiuen-Tsang and I-Tsing wrote on Buddhist pilgrimage, Nalanda and relics.

nindian-history-97-20.s: Kavirajamarga is attributed to the Rashtrakuta ruler:
nindian-history-97-20.x: Amoghavarsha I is credited with the Kavirajamarga.

n80fdff95bae.s: The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea was written by:
n80fdff95bae.x: The Periplus was written in Greek by an anonymous Greek sailor; Ptolemy wrote Geography and Pliny wrote Natural History.

neddd22a8405.s: In stratigraphy, the principle that lower layers are older than the layers above them is called:
neddd22a8405.x: Stratigraphy rests on superposition; counting annual tree rings is dendrochronology.

n73e7e4b2794.s: Mudrarakshasa and Devichandraguptam were written by:
n73e7e4b2794.x: Both plays are by Vishakhadatta; Banabhatta wrote Harshacharita.

nindian-history-1-12.s: The Ayodhya inscription is associated with:
nindian-history-1-12.x: The Ayodhya inscription is associated with Pushyamitra Shunga; Hathigumpha is Kharavela's and Nashik relates to Gautamiputra Satakarni.

nf2b96e56b12.x: The Bhattiprolu inscription refers to the Nigama-sabha; Roman coins were also found at Bhattiprolu.

nc7fd32be5b6.s: The Boghaz-Koi inscription, which names Indra, Varuna, Mitra and Nasatya, belongs to which century BC?
nc7fd32be5b6.x: The Boghaz-Koi inscription from Asia Minor belongs to the fourteenth century BC, not the fourth.

n559deae064c.s: Which of the following is regarded as the first long Sanskrit inscription?
n559deae064c.x: Rudradaman I's Junagadh inscription, which records the repair of the Sudarshana lake, is regarded as the first long Sanskrit inscription.

n090643217f8.s: Masulia, an eastern trading centre mentioned by Ptolemy, is identified with:
n090643217f8.x: Masulia is identified with Machilipatnam on the east coast; Bharukachha, Sopara and Kalyani were Ptolemy's west-coast places.

n36ceb6bfe7a.s: Al-Biruni wrote Kitab-ul-Hind in which language?
n36ceb6bfe7a.x: Al-Biruni, a scholar from Khwarizm who came with Mahmud of Ghazni, wrote Kitab-ul-Hind in Arabic, not Persian.

n39135fca53d.s: The Bhattiprolu stupa was excavated by:
n39135fca53d.x: Alexander Rea excavated Bhattiprolu; Sewell wrote A Forgotten Empire, Burgess worked on Amaravati and Jaggayyapeta, and Elliot dug at Amaravati in 1845.

n40d2556cd0b.s: James Prinsep deciphered the Brahmi script in:

n127bbde64a3.s: The Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela is in which language?
n127bbde64a3.x: The Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela of Kalinga is in Prakrit, in the Brahmi script.

nc50b98533f9.s: Which work calls Yajna Sri Satakarni 'Trisamudradheesvara'?
nc50b98533f9.x: Banabhatta's Harshacharita refers to Yajna Sri Satakarni as Trisamudradheesvara.

ndc2a11d1246.s: Brihatkatha, a source for the Satavahana age, was composed by:
ndc2a11d1246.x: Gunadhya composed the Brihatkatha in Paisachi; it gives information about the Satavahana age.

n2be392430de.s: Which Satavahana ruler is known for re-striking Nahapana's coins?
n2be392430de.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni re-struck Nahapana's coins; ship-motif coins belong to Vasishthiputra Pulumavi and Yajna Sri Satakarni.

n12a9907b2e5.s: The first definite references to coins such as kahapana, nikkha and kamsa occur in:
n12a9907b2e5.x: Pali texts give the first definite references to these coins, and punch-marked coins corroborate them archaeologically.

n3fe3921c3d1.s: Andhranagari, mentioned in the Bhimasena and Serivanija Jatakas, is identified with:
n3fe3921c3d1.x: Andhranagari is identified with Dhanyakataka; P. C. Ray identified its river as the Krishna.

n7625951a33d.s: Sangam texts mainly describe which kingdoms?
n7625951a33d.x: Sangam texts (c. 3rd century BCE - 3rd century CE) describe the Tamil Chera, Chola and Pandya kingdoms.

nindian-history-30-9.s: The earliest known copper plate in India is the:
nindian-history-30-9.x: The Sohgaura plate is the earliest known copper plate and the earliest royal famine-related order.

nindian-history-54-17.x: Ibn Battuta served Muhammad bin Tughlaq; Megasthenes served Chandragupta Maurya.

nap-history-14-5.s: Which Ikshvaku ruler is said to have given away crores of gold coins?
nap-history-14-5.x: The Ikshvaku Santamula I is recorded as having given away crores of gold coins.

nindian-history-1-32.s: The Rabatak inscription, discovered in 1993, is written in the Bactrian language using which script?
nindian-history-1-32.x: The Rabatak inscription is in Bactrian written in the Greek script.

nindian-history-1-13.s: The Sarnath Buddhist Image Inscription (81 AD) is associated with:
nindian-history-1-13.x: The Sarnath Buddhist image inscription is dated to Kanishka's third year, 81 AD.

nindian-history-1-29.s: The Mauryan-era Sohgaura copper plate deals with:
o: Storing food grain for famine or crisis
nindian-history-1-29.x: The Sohgaura copper plate orders grain to be stored for times of famine or crisis.

nindian-history-1-58.s: Which inscription is an early specimen of the Kavya style in Sanskrit?
nindian-history-1-58.x: The Junagadh inscription, the earliest long Sanskrit inscription, is an early specimen of the Kavya style.

nindian-history-54-4.s: Fa-Hien visited India during the reign of:
nindian-history-54-4.x: Fa-Hien, the Buddhist pilgrim, came to India during Chandragupta II's reign.

nindian-history-1-80.s: The Aihole inscription is written in which language?
nindian-history-1-80.x: The Aihole inscription is in Sanskrit, in the Southern Brahmi script.

nindian-history-1-37.s: According to the Aihole inscription, Pulakeshin II stopped Harsha's southward advance at the river:
nindian-history-1-37.x: The Aihole inscription by Ravikirti says Pulakeshin II stopped Harsha at the Narmada, not the Krishna.

n5bce5d8d0b9.s: The inscriptions used as a source for Satavahana history are written in:
n5bce5d8d0b9.x: Satavahana history rests on the Puranas, Prakrit inscriptions and coins; foreign accounts must be cross-checked against these.

n38909a39bf0.s: Which inscription records the Pallava conquest of Vijayapuri?
n38909a39bf0.x: The Manchikallu inscription records the Pallava conquest of Vijayapuri; Mayidavolu records Pallava rule over Andhrapatha.

nap-history-3-16.s: Which inscription is the first to mention Vishnu temples in Andhra?
nap-history-3-16.x: The Pedavegi inscription is the first to mention Vishnu temples in Andhra.

n90e7c8fee7b.s: Attirala, where a hoard of Roman gold coins was found, is in which district?
n90e7c8fee7b.x: Roman gold coin hoards were found at Attirala in Kadapa and Vinukonda in Guntur.

n9af0d0e0db2.s: The Kondamudi copper edict was issued by Jayavarma of which dynasty?
n9af0d0e0db2.x: Jayavarma of the Brihatpalayanas, whose capital was Koduru, issued it in his 10th regnal year.

n9bf9552b8ef.s: The Gurazala inscription belongs to the last phase of which dynasty?
n9bf9552b8ef.x: The Gurazala inscription belongs to the last phase of the Ikshvaku dynasty.

nfdd28b2b114.s: The Bhattiprolu relic caskets are associated with the pre-Satavahana ruler:
nfdd28b2b114.x: The caskets belong to the pre-Satavahana ruler Kubiraka; Bhattiprolu is the oldest stupa in Andhra Pradesh.

n9105ba0f501.s: The Ikshvaku ruler Rudrapurushadatta was defeated by:
n9105ba0f501.x: Pallava Simhavarman defeated Rudrapurushadatta; the Pallavas then held the land south of the Krishna and the Brihatpalayanas the land to its north.

nf35f002e255.s: Gathasaptasati, a Prakrit work of 700 verses, was composed by:
nf35f002e255.x: Hala's Gathasaptasati is a Prakrit work of 700 verses that records early Telugu words.

n2620d20f01c.s: The Naneghat inscription was issued by:
n2620d20f01c.x: Queen Naganika, wife of Satakarni I, issued the Naneghat inscription recording Vedic sacrifices and gifts to Brahmins.

nf800c4d45fd.s: Gautami Balasri's Nasik inscription belongs to the reign of:
nf800c4d45fd.x: Issued during Vasishthiputra Pulumavi's reign, it records Gautamiputra Satakarni's victories and titles.

n7ad61e5e789.s: According to the Matsya Purana, how many Satavahana kings ruled?
n7ad61e5e789.x: The Matsya Purana mentions 30 Satavahana kings ruling for 456 years.

n1784132bdc8.s: Which Andhra habitation mound also had a mint?
n1784132bdc8.x: Kondapur was a habitation mound and a mint; Gudiwada Dibba is a habitation mound of the Mauryan to Satavahana period.

nap-history-3-5.s: The Brihatpalayanas were feudatories of the:
nap-history-3-5.x: The Brihatpalayanas were feudatories of the Ikshvakus; the Kondamudi copper plate is the only record of the dynasty.

nap-history-3-4.s: Which ruler of Vengi is mentioned in Samudragupta's Allahabad Pillar inscription?
nap-history-3-4.x: The Allahabad Pillar inscription names Hastivarman of Vengi (Salankayana) among the southern kings Samudragupta defeated.

nap-history-3-21.s: The Eluru inscription, which mentions 'Munyada', was issued by:
nap-history-3-21.x: The Eluru inscription was issued by Devavarma; Nandivarman II issued the Kolleru inscription.

o: A king granting a village or land to Brahmins, often with tax exemptions
A village council issuing military orders to the king
A merchant guild granting Roman coins to foreign traders
A Buddhist monk listing donors without fiscal details
n2db72ec83bc.x: Copper-plate grants generally record a king granting a village or land to Brahmins, together with tax exemptions.

nb37f6f6bc8d.s: A megalithic burial in the form of a table-like chamber made of large slabs is called a:
nb37f6f6bc8d.x: A dolmen is a table-like chamber; a cist is a stone-slab box, a menhir an upright stone and a sarcophagus a clay coffin.

n3ae1ae2d301.s: Upper Palaeolithic cave art at Bhimbetka has been found in about how many caves and shelters?
n3ae1ae2d301.x: Upper Palaeolithic art at Bhimbetka occurs in about 300 caves and shelters.

nindian-history-137-9.s: The Chalcolithic horizon at Daimabad shows links with the:
nindian-history-137-9.x: Daimabad shows a Chalcolithic horizon with Late Harappan links; Inamgaon is Jorwe and Ahar is the Ahar/Banas type site.

ncb2dc4c8393.s: Which Andhra Pradesh site is known for well-made quartzite blades?
ncb2dc4c8393.x: Yerragondapalem is known for quartzite blades; Kurnool caves and Jwalapuram are Upper Palaeolithic sites.

n3c50022b20c.s: The microlith centres of Andhra Pradesh such as Giddaluru and Kondapur were discovered by:
n3c50022b20c.x: Robert Bruce Foote discovered the AP microlith centres; N. R. Banerji is the leading researcher of megaliths.

nf4bd5885343.s: Black-and-red ware has been found at all Andhra megalithic sites except:
nf4bd5885343.x: Black-and-red ware was found at all Andhra sites except Visakhapatnam.

ne9bb546e344.s: The Ahar and Kayatha Chalcolithic cultures were contemporaries of the:
ne9bb546e344.x: Ahar and Kayatha were contemporaries of the Harappans; other Chalcolithic cultures were post-Harappan.

need7a8df4b4.s: Bhimbetka was discovered by V. S. Wakankar in:
need7a8df4b4.x: V. S. Wakankar discovered Bhimbetka, near Bhopal, in 1957; it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2003.

nde9ead6b340.s: The Middle Palaeolithic is principally a ____-tool stage.
nde9ead6b340.x: The Middle Palaeolithic is a flake-tool stage; microliths belong to the Upper Palaeolithic and Mesolithic.

nindian-history-137-16.s: Which of the following Chalcolithic sites is NOT in Maharashtra?
nindian-history-137-16.x: Kayatha is in Madhya Pradesh; Jorwe, Savalda and Inamgaon are in Maharashtra.

n189dc615718.s: In 1842 Meadows Taylor found a stone axe at:
n189dc615718.x: Meadows Taylor's 1842 stone axe was found at Lingasugur, not Jwalapuram.

n97b9bff4a05.s: The animal most commonly painted in rock art is the:
n97b9bff4a05.x: The deer is the most commonly painted animal, not the elephant.

nindian-history-137-14.s: The Jorwe culture, known for village farming settlements, belongs to:
nindian-history-137-14.x: The Jorwe culture belongs to Maharashtra, not Madhya Pradesh.

ncd771fe3160.s: About how many types of megalithic burials have been identified in Andhra Pradesh?
ncd771fe3160.x: About twelve types of megalithic burials are noted in AP; N. R. Banerji is associated with their study.

nb448d1e3b20.s: Handaxes, cleavers and choppers of quartzite are characteristic of the:
nb448d1e3b20.x: Lower Palaeolithic tools were handaxes, cleavers and choppers; flakes are Middle Palaeolithic and blades Upper Palaeolithic.

na79cb04b78a.s: Giddaluru, the key microlithic centre of Andhra Pradesh, is in which district?
na79cb04b78a.x: Giddaluru is in Prakasam district; Nagarjunakonda, Kondapur and Khammam are other microlithic centres.

nebdb8934095.s: AMS dating at Mayiladumparai places the beginning of the Iron Age in South India at about:
nebdb8934095.x: Mayiladumparai AMS dating puts the South Indian Iron Age at about 2100 BCE, earlier than the Gangetic Iron Age.

nf4a0b3ec6e3.s: Which Andhra site is known for Chalcolithic painted pottery?
nf4a0b3ec6e3.x: Patapadu has Chalcolithic painted pottery; Keesarapalli is known for copper tools.

n475b789e801.s: Palaeolithic tools of the Kadapa–Kurnool region were mainly made of:
n475b789e801.x: Quartzite was characteristic of Kadapa and Kurnool tools, whereas limestone was used north of the Krishna.

n8c2548f2860.s: Which Early Harappan site shows a transition to the Mature Harappan phase and later Jhangar traces?
n8c2548f2860.x: Amri shows the pre-Harappan to Mature Harappan transition, rhinoceros remains and later Jhangar traces.

n7f4943ead5c.s: Which scholar suggested that the Harappan Civilisation arose through migration from Sumer?
n7f4943ead5c.x: Mackay suggested migration from Sumer; Marshall proposed indigenous evolution and Wheeler diffusion from West Asia.

n3dae48589b4.s: The main domesticated animals of the Neolithic phase of Baluchistan and the Indus plains were:
n3dae48589b4.x: The animals were sheep and goats, not horses and camels; crops included wheat, barley, dates and cotton.

nf6fb9afb123.s: Kili Gul Muhammad, an early farming village, lies in which valley?
nf6fb9afb123.x: Kili Gul Muhammad is in the Quetta valley; Rana Ghundai is in the Zhob-Loralai valley.

n31bf98b6d9b.s: Which of the following was already known in the Early Harappan phase?
n31bf98b6d9b.x: Copper, the wheel and the plough were already known in the Early Harappan phase, along with granaries and defence walls.

n99ff209adc6.s: Mehrgarh, with the earliest evidence of agriculture in the subcontinent, lies near which pass?
n99ff209adc6.x: Mehrgarh is in Baluchistan near the Bolan Pass and begins c. 7000 BCE.

n827f0d70365.s: The pottery of Kalibangan is classified into how many fabrics?
n827f0d70365.x: Kalibangan's pottery is classified into six fabrics; the settlement was enclosed by a mud-brick fortification.

n0eeb97ef526.s: The Early Harappan phase (3300–2600 BCE) is called the:
n0eeb97ef526.x: The Early Harappan phase, corresponding to the Hakra phase, is the Regionalisation Era, not the Integration Era.

nded5ae6ec83.s: At Mehrgarh, the dead were usually buried:
o: Under or near houses, often flexed, with grave goods
In large public monuments without objects
Only after cremation outside the settlement
Only in stone chambers far from habitation
nded5ae6ec83.x: Mehrgarh burials were under or near houses, often flexed, with ornaments, tools and sometimes goats.

n7ee00b44d4f.s: Which of the following is NOT an Early Harappan regional pottery tradition?
n7ee00b44d4f.x: The Early Harappan traditions are Amri, Kot Diji, Sothi-Siswal and Hakra wares; Northern Black Polished Ware is not one of them.

n8284f071d87.s:
Assertion (A): Dholavira was the first Indus Valley Civilisation site in India to be inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Reason (R): Dholavira became India's 40th UNESCO World Heritage Site.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n8284f071d87.x: Both are true, but being India's 40th site does not explain why it was the first IVC site listed; it is also Gujarat's fourth such site.

nindian-history-137-19.s: The Harappan settlement of Banawali is in:
nindian-history-137-19.x: Banawali is a Harappan site in Haryana; Rangpur is a Late Harappan site in Gujarat.

n92a81103255.s: The Mature Harappan phase is dated to:
n92a81103255.x: The Mature phase is 2600–1900 BCE; 3300–2600 BCE is Early Harappan and 1900–1300 BCE Late Harappan.

n8bb1cab538d.s: The Harappan site of Mandi is in which district of Uttar Pradesh?
n8bb1cab538d.x: Mandi is in Muzaffarnagar; Rakhigarhi is in Hisar, Banawali in the Hisar–Fatehabad region and Dholavira in Kutch.

nindian-history-2-11.x: B. P. Bopardikar discovered Daimabad in 1958; Sharma excavated Ropar, Joshi Manda and Bisht Dholavira.

nindian-history-2-4.x: Daya Ram Sahni excavated Harappa in 1921; R. D. Banerjee worked at Mohenjo-daro in 1922.

nindian-history-26-2-5.x: Burzahom is known for pit dwellings; Sinauli for 125 burials and Banawali for a toy terracotta plough.

nindian-history-3-26.s: The bronze buffalo was found at:
nindian-history-3-26.x: Daimabad yielded the bronze buffalo; Ropar had a dog buried with humans and Banawali a large quantity of barley.

n112e027a70b.x: J. P. Joshi excavated Surkotada; Bisht excavated Banawali and Sharma Ropar.

nindian-history-3-58.s: A signboard of ten Indus signs was found at:
nindian-history-3-58.x: The ten-sign signboard is from Dholavira; Lothal has the dockyard and Kalibangan the ploughed field.

nindian-history-2-20.s: Which Harappan site is associated with the procurement of Himalayan wood?
nindian-history-2-20.x: Manda is linked with Himalayan wood; Daimabad with bronze objects and Dholavira with reservoirs.

n348801997aa.s: The southernmost Harappan boundary site is:
n348801997aa.x: Daimabad is the southern boundary site; Manda is northern, Alamgirpur eastern and Sutkagendor western.

nindian-history-26-2-20.s: Harappa is situated on the bank of which river?
nindian-history-26-2-20.x: Harappa lies on the Ravi; Mohenjo-daro is on the Indus, Ropar on the Sutlej and Manda on the Chenab.

nindian-history-3-35.s: The earliest evidence of a furnace comes from the Harappan site of:
nindian-history-3-35.x: Kot Bala gives the earliest furnace evidence; Amri gave rhinoceros remains and Lothal a copper dog.

nindian-history-3-28.s: A terracotta toy plough and an oval settlement with radial streets are associated with:
nindian-history-3-28.x: Banawali yielded a terracotta plough model and Mother Goddess figurines, and had an oval settlement.

nindian-history-3-59.x: The Great Bath is at Mohenjo-daro; Lothal has a graveyard and Kalibangan the ploughed field.

n246efb13b7f.s: Which of the following Harappan sites is located in India rather than Pakistan?
n246efb13b7f.x: Lothal is in Gujarat, India; Harappa, Mohenjodaro and Chanhudaro are in Pakistan.

nindian-history-3-52.s: Skeletons found in wells are associated with which Harappan site?
nindian-history-3-52.x: Skeletons in wells, the humped bull seal and an ivory weight balance are linked with Mohenjo-daro.

nindian-history-3-60.s: Which Harappan site shows evidence of an earthquake?
nindian-history-3-60.x: Kalibangan shows earthquake evidence, along with a ploughed field, fire altars and a Mesopotamian-type cylinder seal.

nindian-history-3-78.s: Which Harappan site in Saurashtra yielded rice, bajra and sorghum?
nindian-history-3-78.x: Rangpur in Saurashtra yielded rice, bajra and sorghum.

nindian-history-2-5.s: The 1935–36 excavation that revealed a bead-making factory and furnace was at:
nindian-history-2-5.x: Chanhudaro revealed a bead-making factory and furnace; Ropar lies on the Sutlej and Daimabad yielded bronze objects.

nindian-history-3-11.x: Daimabad lies on the Pravara, a tributary of the Godavari, not on the Narmada.

nindian-history-3-5.s: Kalibangan lies on the bank of the:
nindian-history-3-5.x: Kalibangan lies on the Ghaggar; the Bhogava is Lothal's river.

nindian-history-3-22.s: Rice husk, a copper dog and three double burials are associated with:
nindian-history-3-22.x: Lothal yielded rice husk, a Persian Gulf seal, three double burials and a copper dog.

n49162fa1537.s: Who described the ruins of Harappa during 1826–38?
n49162fa1537.x: Charles Masson described the ruins in 1826–38; Fleet published seals in 1912 and Sahni found Harappa in 1921–22.

nf1c5968b260.s: The westernmost Harappan coastal town is:
nf1c5968b260.x: Sutkagendor is the westernmost Harappan coastal town.

nindian-history-3-31.s: Manda, a base for procuring Himalayan timber, lies on which river?
nindian-history-3-31.x: Manda on the Chenab procured Himalayan timber, which was floated downstream to other Harappan towns.

n7c18f8cd305.s: The Harappan site of Alamgirpur in Meerut lies on which river?
n7c18f8cd305.x: Alamgirpur is on the Hindon in Meerut, Uttar Pradesh.

nindian-history-3-4.s: The first Harappan site excavated in independent India was:
nindian-history-3-4.x: Ropar (Rupnagar) on the Sutlej in Punjab was the first Harappan site excavated after Independence.

nindian-history-3-77.s: How many urban divisions did Dholavira have?
nindian-history-3-77.x: Dholavira had three divisions: Citadel, Middle Town and Lower Town.

nindian-history-3-71.s: Mandi in Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh, is known for a Harappan:
nindian-history-3-71.x: Mandi is known for a Harappan jewellery hoard found in 2000.

nindian-history-3-74.s: Shortughai, a Harappan trade outpost for lapis lazuli, is in:
nindian-history-3-74.x: Shortughai is in Afghanistan; Kerala-no-dhoro, a salt centre, is in Gujarat.

n1f265c44627.s: The Rigvedic period is broadly characterised as:
n1f265c44627.x: In the comparison, the Indus Valley was urban, the Rigvedic period pastoral, the Later Vedic agrarian and the Medieval based on landlordism.

n7938cd7a85a.s: The Harappan Civilisation is estimated to have covered about:
n7938cd7a85a.x: It covered about 1.3 million square kilometres with about five million people.

n7ef6970d5cc.s: Which of the following was NOT among the five iconic archaeological sites named in the Union Budget 2020?
n7ef6970d5cc.x: The five sites were Rakhigarhi, Hastinapur, Shivsagar, Dholavira and Adichanallur; Mohenjodaro was not included.

n43ea803cb51.s: The Harappan site of Hulas is in which state?
n43ea803cb51.x: Hulas is in Saharanpur and Mandi in Muzaffarnagar, both in Uttar Pradesh.

nindian-history-2-7.s: Alexander Cunningham visited Harappa, before the 1921 excavations, in:
nindian-history-2-7.x: Cunningham saw pottery, tools and a seal at Harappa in 1853 and 1856 but did not grasp their significance.

nae3966b7f5e.x: Rakhigarhi is in Haryana, not Rajasthan; Kalibangan is the Rajasthan site.

ndd9dfd80dd8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Indus Valley cities?
o: No palaces or temples have been clearly identified in them
Their drainage was more advanced than that of contemporary Mesopotamia and Egypt
Their standardised urban planning suggests a civic authority
The absence of identified palaces or temples proves there was no civic authority
ndd9dfd80dd8.x: The absence of clearly identified palaces or temples does not disprove civic authority; standardised planning instead suggests it.

nf7352fe7bfa.s: Which of the following pairs about the Harappan street plan is correctly matched?
o: Width of main streets – About 10 metres (30 feet)
Angle at which streets crossed – 45 degrees
Direction of main streets – Radial from the centre
Pattern formed by streets – Concentric rings
nf7352fe7bfa.x: Main Harappan streets were about 30 feet (10 metres) wide; streets ran north–south and east–west, crossing at right angles to form blocks.

nd16914cf0b1.s: Covered Harappan drains were provided with ____ for cleaning.
nd16914cf0b1.x: Covered drains had manholes for maintenance and were built of burnt bricks and terracotta pipes.

n99c4a5defd9.s: Which Harappan site used sandstone and limestone blocks as an exception to brick construction?
n99c4a5defd9.x: Burnt bricks were common and mud bricks were used at Kalibangan; Dholavira was the exception with stone blocks.

ncce3069e3fd.s: Giant reservoirs fed by bunds, check-dams and channels are a feature of:
ncce3069e3fd.x: Dholavira had giant reservoirs supplied through bunds, check-dams and channels, with dams and embankments.

na53bba7da44.s: Which Harappan site had its citadel and lower town within one enclosure?
na53bba7da44.x: Lothal had both divisions in one enclosure; Kalibangan had a fortified lower town.

nindian-history-3-18.x: Harappa yielded Cemetery H, a coffin burial, wheat and barley in a wooden mortar, and dice.

nindian-history-3-24.s: A stadium-like structure is associated with which Harappan site?
nindian-history-3-24.x: Dholavira had a stadium-like open ground and special cemetery structures.

nindian-history-3-46.s: How many rooms did the Harappan granary have?
nindian-history-3-46.x: The Harappa granary had two rows of six rooms each, giving 12 rooms.

nced633c9563.s: Which Harappan city had reservoirs partly cut into the rock?
nced633c9563.x: Some Dholavira reservoirs were partly cut into the rock and it used sandstone and limestone blocks, unlike baked-brick Mohenjodaro and Harappa.

nb984eb9d761.s: Harappan granaries are generally interpreted as:
nb984eb9d761.x: Granaries are commonly read as stores of agricultural surplus, though this interpretation is debated.

nadcee85e719.s: Which small Harappan settlement had wooden drains?
nadcee85e719.x: Kalibangan had wooden drains, while Banawali lacked a systematic drainage system.

n6b226c0aab1.s: Radial streets are a distinctive town-planning feature of:
n6b226c0aab1.x: Banawali is noted for radial streets and no systematic drainage; Dholavira had three parts and Chanhudaro no citadel.

n19f87cadcc1.s: In Harappan cities, the raised and fortified citadel usually lay on the:
n19f87cadcc1.x: The citadel stood on a raised, fortified platform on the west, with the lower town to the east.

nb7633684b45.s: Which Harappan site has yielded the largest number of wells?
nb7633684b45.x: Mohenjodaro has the most wells; Dholavira relied on reservoirs and Lothal had a tidal dockyard.

naf5b2c5cda5.s: The red sandstone male torso was found at:
naf5b2c5cda5.x: The red sandstone male torso is from Harappa; the Pashupati seal is from Mohenjodaro, the ship seal from Lothal and carts with seated drivers from Chanhudaro.

n7213065adee.s: The most common motif on Harappan seals is the:
n7213065adee.x: The unicorn is the most common Harappan seal motif, and the pipal the most depicted tree.

nb6858b13a3d.s: Which of the following is among the five largest Harappan cities?
nb6858b13a3d.x: The five largest are Mohenjodaro, Harappa, Ganweriwala, Rakhigarhi and Dholavira.

o: An animal motif with an inscription
nc103fdb8efe.x: Rectangular seals carry only inscriptions, while square seals combine an animal motif with an inscription.

n90ddff6943a.s: Nageshwar and Balakot were Harappan centres of:
n90ddff6943a.x: Shell work was concentrated at Nageshwar, Balakot and Lothal; bead-making at Chanhudaro, Lothal and Kalibangan.

nindian-history-38-10.s: Which Harappan crop was connected with textiles and trade?
nindian-history-38-10.x: Cotton was the Harappan textile crop.

nb3d8c11a0af.s: The Harappan copper scale was found at:
nb3d8c11a0af.x: The copper scale is from Harappa; the shell scale from Mohenjodaro and the ivory scale from Lothal.

nb7c648254a1.s: Camel bones have been found at the Harappan site of:
nb7c648254a1.x: Camel bones were found at Kalibangan; Ropar had a dog buried with a human and Amri rhinoceros remains.

nd65d33343f9.s: Evidence of well irrigation in the Harappan civilisation comes from:
nd65d33343f9.x: Well irrigation is known from Allahdino; Dholavira had reservoirs and Banawali a terracotta plough model.

n53e2f3aff33.s: Harappan seals, beads and weights have been reported from all of the following EXCEPT:
n53e2f3aff33.x: They are reported from Oman, Bahrain, Iraq and Iran, but not from Egypt.

n494cbf7df4b.s: Controversial horse bones dated to about 2000 BCE are claimed from:
n494cbf7df4b.x: The Surkotada horse bones are claimed to date to about 2000 BCE, but their identification is not widely accepted.

n974eee00fd4.s: The Harappans obtained lapis lazuli from:
n974eee00fd4.x: Lapis lazuli came from Badakhshan through Shortughai; copper came from Khetri and Oman, and gold from Kolar and Afghanistan.

nacd6bee9594.s: Failaka, where Indus seals have been found, is in present-day:
nacd6bee9594.x: Indus seals have been found at Susa, Ur, Nippur, Failaka (Kuwait) and Bahrain.

n07510b645de.s: Harappan urbanisation rested on all of the following EXCEPT:
n07510b645de.x: Farm surplus, trade networks, craft specialisation and standard weights created urbanisation; iron was unknown to the Harappans.

ne36c1d07099.x: Sutkagendor was the westernmost, not the easternmost, Harappan site.

n6d627c87245.s: Which of the following was an import, not an export, in Harappan external trade?
n6d627c87245.x: Carnelian beads, ivory, timber and cotton were exports; silver was imported.

ndae12627ff6.s: The Greeks referred to cotton as:
ndae12627ff6.x: The Greeks called cotton Sindon; Mehrgarh gives Neolithic evidence of cotton.

n98fed4523f6.s: Which of the following has NOT been found at Harappan sites?
n98fed4523f6.x: Spindle-whorls occur widely in houses and cotton and wool were used, but no spinning wheels have been found.

n8ca449490c5.s: Chert blades from which place show that the Harappans kept using stone tools alongside metal?
n8ca449490c5.x: Chert blades from Rohri show stone tools continued alongside metal tools.

n720c71900d4.s: At Harappa, the granaries were arranged in two rows of ____ structures each.
n720c71900d4.x: The Harappa granaries had two rows of six structures for storing surplus.

n64756c694a3.s: The Lothal dockyard was excavated in 1954 by:
n64756c694a3.x: S. R. Rao excavated the brick-lined Lothal dockyard (about 218 m x 37 m) in 1954.

n46baac9c701.s: Which of the following was a wild animal, not a domesticated one, for the Harappans?
n46baac9c701.x: Dog, cat, ass, camel, sheep and goat were domesticated; elephant and tiger were wild.

n406ddba3c7b.x: Meluhha meant the Indus region; Dilmun was Bahrain and Magan was Oman or Makran.

ne52ab973376.s: Which metal was unknown to the Harappans?
ne52ab973376.x: Iron was unknown to the Harappans; copper, bronze, gold, silver and lead were used.

na584cf3d969.s: Harappan bronze was made by combining copper with:
na584cf3d969.x: Bronze was copper with tin, used for tools, weapons and the Dancing Girl.

n028a5025450.s: Which form of irrigation in the Indus Valley Civilisation remains inconclusive?
n028a5025450.x: Wells at Allahdino, reservoirs at Dholavira and flood irrigation are evidenced, but canal irrigation is inconclusive.

n58ea77de544.s: Which animal was not known to the Mature Harappans in the generally accepted view?
n58ea77de544.x: The horse was not known to the Mature Harappans; the Surkotada horse bones are controversial.

n23f54912793.s: Which of the following was NOT a use of Harappan seals?
n23f54912793.x: Seals were used for sealing, authentication, ownership and identity, not for minting coins.

nc38866c0efb.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Harappan seals?
o: Square seals generally carry an animal figure with an inscription
Rectangular seals generally carry only an inscription
Mesopotamian-type cylinder seals were common at all Harappan sites
The unicorn is the most common seal motif
nc38866c0efb.x: Mesopotamian-type cylinder seals were rare, not common, at Harappan sites.

n96287c57cae.s: An average Harappan inscription contains about how many signs?
n96287c57cae.x: The average inscription has about five signs; around 5,000 inscribed objects are known and the script is undeciphered.

na80530b51f9.s: Harappan weights were generally ____ in shape.
na80530b51f9.x: Harappan weights were generally cubical, mostly of chert, not spherical.

n3500296503a.s: Harappan seals were mostly made of:
n3500296503a.x: Harappan seals were mostly of steatite and generally square.

n543378b98db.s: Dholavira, excavated by R. S. Bisht in 1990, was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in:
n543378b98db.x: Dholavira was listed in 2021 and is the only Harappan site on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

ndd80574848c.s: Which of the following pairs about Harappan settlement layout is correctly matched?
o: Lower town – Northern side of the city
Lower town – Public buildings and elite areas
Citadel – Western side of the city
ndd80574848c.x: The citadel lay to the west with public and elite areas, while the eastern lower town held commoners' houses.

nfbc4023cf2a.s: The centralised-state view of Harappan polity rests mainly on:
o: Identification of Harappa as the capital
nfbc4023cf2a.x: The centralised-state view rests on uniformity over a huge area; no single capital has been identified.

ndce882ac48e.s: Caste is considered to have crystallised in the:
ndce882ac48e.x: Caste crystallised in the Later Vedic period; there is no textual evidence of a rigid Harappan caste system.

n759bc1417b1.s: Which aspect of Harappan clothing is NOT supported by evidence?
n759bc1417b1.x: Cotton, wool, upper and lower garments and the Priest-King's shawl are supported, but there is no evidence of stitching.

n126f1eb48dd.s: Harappan maces, axes and spears were made of:
n126f1eb48dd.x: Harappan weapons were few and simple and made of copper and bronze; no horse-drawn chariots are known.

nd6b733d2967.s: A Harappan toy factory has been found at:
nd6b733d2967.x: Chanhudaro had a toy factory; cubical dice come from Harappa and the toys were of terracotta.

n5a0030d5566.s: Lipstick is associated with which Harappan site?
n5a0030d5566.x: Chanhudaro is associated with lipstick; bronze mirrors, ivory combs and collyrium sticks were also used.

ne1a8ca45866.s: Grave goods such as pottery, ornaments and mirrors in Harappan burials are taken to indicate belief in:
ne1a8ca45866.x: Grave goods indicate belief in an afterlife and differences in status, not exclusive cremation.

neeb151edec6.s: Extended burials, pot burials and circular pits with grave goods but no skeleton are reported from:
neeb151edec6.x: Kalibangan has yielded all three burial types.

n672e3135aeb.s: Standardised bricks, binary weights, uniform seals and grid-plan towns over a large area suggest that the Harappans had:
n672e3135aeb.x: Widespread standardisation is the main basis for inferring a significant degree of central authority.

n9d9d54c2e79.s: Harappan social stratification and polity are reconstructed mainly from:
n9d9d54c2e79.x: Interpretations rely on material remains, as the script gives no names of rulers.

n89b84e257dc.s: Harappan political structure, for which there is no clear-cut evidence, is described as appearing:
n89b84e257dc.x: The polity appears corporate; monarchy, theocracy or a single capital are not conclusively established.

n98943488e2e.s: Fractional burial at Mohenjodaro and Harappa involved:
o: Placing ashes in an urn after cremation
Burying the complete body in a coffin
Burying a human together with a dog
Burying bones after exposure of the body
n98943488e2e.x: Fractional burial meant burying the bones after the body had been exposed.

nb967023ce50.s: A gemstone factory with over 3,000 semi-precious stones was found at:
nb967023ce50.x: Rakhigarhi had the gemstone factory; Chanhudaro had a bead-making factory and Lothal bead workshops.

n635e6d376ca.s: The only Indus city without a citadel is:
n635e6d376ca.x: Chanhudaro is the only Indus city without a citadel; Indus glazed pottery has been described as the world's first.

ne961d7c9370.s: Gold and silver necklaces of the Indus civilisation were found at:
ne961d7c9370.x: Gold and silver necklaces were found at Allahdino; Rakhigarhi had a gold foundry with an active furnace.

n600ae096f7f.x: Carnelian came from Saurashtra, and carnelian beads made at Lothal were exported to Mesopotamia and the Persian Gulf.

naea801bc8e8.s: The lost-wax technique of metal casting is also known as:
naea801bc8e8.x: Lost-wax or cire perdue: a clay-coated wax model is heated, the wax melts out and molten metal is poured in.

n56ab91358c4.s: Which of the following is NOT among the Indus terracotta figurines and toys?
n56ab91358c4.x: Iron horse-drawn chariots are not found; the other three are Indus terracotta figures and toys.

n1c39d0103ee.s: Differences in house size, burial goods and ornaments in the Indus Valley Civilisation indicate:
n1c39d0103ee.x: These differences indicate social stratification; the four-fold division is speculative.

n82fac714ba2.s: The Great Bath at Mohenjodaro is associated with:
n82fac714ba2.x: The Great Bath is associated with ritual purification.

n1958af7741f.s: The bronze Dancing Girl was excavated in 1926 by:
n1958af7741f.x: Ernest Mackay excavated it in 1926 under John Marshall; it belongs to the Mature Harappan phase, c. 2500 BCE.

ne35f9f60d01.s: Harappan bangles were commonly made of:
ne35f9f60d01.x: Shell bangles were used; ornaments were of gold, silver, beads and shell, and mirrors and combs were known.

n183b181ce69.s: Who identified the Pashupati seal figure as Proto-Shiva?
n183b181ce69.x: John Marshall proposed the Proto-Shiva or Pashupati reading, which remains debated.

n5329ce0b51a.s: Harappan Mother Goddess worship has a later parallel in:
n5329ce0b51a.x: Mother Goddess worship parallels the later Shakti cults; the Kalibangan fire altar link with Vedic yajna is debated.

n3ca805b68c7.x: Harappan religion was nature- and fertility-oriented; the later Vedic religion was sacrificial and ritualistic.

n819fdfb9a8b.s: The pipal motif in the Indus Valley Civilisation goes back to the:
n819fdfb9a8b.x: The pipal motif is traced to the Early Harappan phase, and pipal worship continued in later Indian religion.

nindian-history-42-16.x: Bharat Mata is Abanindranath Tagore's 1905 painting; Lakshmi appears on Muhammad Ghori's coins.

n8c95b0170bb.s: Mother Goddess figurines and the male Pashupati figure show that the Harappans worshipped:
n8c95b0170bb.x: Mother Goddess figurines and the Pashupati figure show worship of both; no palaces, temples or horse-drawn chariots are known.

nindian-history-41-8.s: The entire 9th Mandala of the Rigveda is devoted to:
nindian-history-41-8.x: Soma has the whole 9th Mandala; Indra is the warrior god, Vishnu holds the Chakra and Saraswati the Veena.

nindian-history-41-14.s: In the Rigveda, Varuna is associated with:
nindian-history-41-14.x: Varuna upholds cosmic order; Agni is god of fire and sacrifice and Indra the warrior god.

nindian-history-41-17.s: The worship of Rama and Sita is associated with:
nindian-history-41-17.x: Rama and Sita are linked with Ramananda; Chaitanya preached Krishna Bhakti and Guru Nanak worshipped the Nirgun Brahma.

ne027c59323c.s: The proto-Shiva reading of the Pashupati seal is treated cautiously mainly because:
o: The seal belongs to the Vedic period
The seal is a Mesopotamian import
The seal was found at Lothal
ne027c59323c.x: Since the Harappan script is undeciphered, the religious meaning of the seal is not conclusively established.

n343368fdaf8.s: Harappan fire altars, whose link with Vedic yajna is debated, have been found at:
n343368fdaf8.x: Kalibangan has fire altars; their connection with later Vedic yajna remains debated, not conclusive.

n394e38d5312.s: Rig Vedic religion was centred on:
o: Male nature gods and open-air yajnas
n394e38d5312.x: Rig Vedic religion had male nature gods such as Indra, Agni and Varuna and open-air yajnas; Harappan religion was fertility-oriented.

n5b668b83b8d.s: The current consensus on the decline of the Harappan civilisation favours:
n5b668b83b8d.x: The consensus rejects a single sudden catastrophe and favours a gradual decline driven by climate, rivers, ecology, trade and urban failure.

n7f557f8a10e.s: The Deoria Tal pollen evidence from Uttarakhand indicates that the 4.2 ka event saw a:
n7f557f8a10e.x: Deoria Tal pollen and AMS-dated Trapa seed cases indicate a sharp weakening of the monsoon, not a strengthening.

nec62895709b.s: Which Harappan site was flooded several times?
nec62895709b.x: Chanhudaro was flooded several times, and the shifting Indus led to the abandonment of sites like Mohenjodaro.

n18822f8e532.s: Which of the following was absent in the Mature Harappan phase but became important later?
n18822f8e532.x: Horse, chariot and iron were absent in the Mature Harappan phase; fire altars, pipal worship and burials are cited as continuities.

n34b8a3a2aa7.s: The invasion theory of Harappan decline, now rejected, is associated with:
n34b8a3a2aa7.x: Wheeler's invasion theory is rejected for lack of evidence, the later date of the Rig Veda and reinterpretation of the skeletons.

nff24e48ee82.s: Which of the following became more important during the Late Harappan phase?
nff24e48ee82.x: In the Late Harappan phase seals, script, weights and trade declined, bricks lost uniformity and local farming grew in importance.

nfc3aba08290.s: Ecological imbalance as a cause of the Harappan decline is associated with:
nfc3aba08290.x: Fairservis argued ecological imbalance; Lambrick the Indus shift, Raikes tectonic change and Agrawal Ghaggar-Hakra drying.

ndd3ad119841.s: Deforestation, soil salinity and overgrazing are cited as ____ causes of the Harappan decline.
ndd3ad119841.x: Deforestation, soil salinity, overgrazing and exhaustion of copper and timber are ecological and resource stresses.

nc1ed30ad479.s: In the Late Harappan phase, pottery became:
nc1ed30ad479.x: Late Harappan pottery became more regionally varied; stone and copper tools continued without complex-cast metal objects.

n83d2eff27d6.s: Floods as the cause of the Harappan decline are associated with:
o: Mortimer Wheeler, Gordon Childe and Stuart Piggott
Aurel Stein and A. N. Ghosh
John Marshall, E. Mackay and S. R. Rao
n83d2eff27d6.x: Marshall, Mackay and Rao are linked with floods; Wheeler, Childe and Piggott with invasion, Stein and Ghosh with drought and Lambrick with the Indus shift.

n2b9289271de.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Harappan and Rigvedic cultural features?
o: Rigvedic culture transmitted ideas mainly through seals and script
Harappan settlements were urban and planned
The Rigvedic horse was domesticated and central to warfare
Rigvedic warriors used a coat of mail and helmet
n2b9289271de.x: Seals and script are the Harappan, not the Rigvedic, means of transmission.

n05464b4d5ba.s: Which of the following scholars is a proponent of the Indigenous ('Out of India') theory?
n05464b4d5ba.x: S. R. Rao, B. B. Lal and Shrikant Talageri back the indigenous theory, a marginal view; Max Muller, Wheeler and Parpola back migration.

n7942db5de8a.s: The Swat valley culture known for horse remains and new burial practices is the:
n7942db5de8a.x: This is the Gandhara Grave culture; BMAC lay in Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and north Afghanistan.

n29881829ce8.s: The domesticated horse was central to warfare in the:
n29881829ce8.x: The horse was central to Rigvedic warfare, while the Harappan civilisation shows no such evidence.

nf20112d7ae3.s: The oldest Iranian (Zoroastrian) text, closely parallel to the Rigveda, is the:
nf20112d7ae3.x: The Avesta is the oldest Zoroastrian text and points to a common Indo-Iranian stock with the Rigveda.

nc67430db23d.s: Which haplogroup is discussed in the genetic evidence for the migration theory?
nc67430db23d.x: The migration theory uses linguistics, Rigvedic geography, horse and chariot archaeology and genetics, including R1a.

nc84bb0686b2.s: According to Iranian literature, which group was a branch of the early Aryans?
nc84bb0686b2.x: The Dasas were a branch of early Aryans, while the Dasyus were original inhabitants.

nd4b9f1436c0.s: The Dardic branch of the Indo-European family is associated with:
nd4b9f1436c0.x: Dardic is associated with Jammu and Kashmir; Iranian lies outside India and Indo-Aryan is another branch.

n605faa85713.s: The Boghazkoi inscription, a Hittite-Mitanni treaty, dates to about the:
n605faa85713.x: The Boghazkoi treaty from Anatolia dates to about the 14th century BCE (c. 1400 BCE), not CE.

ndd73861c963.s: Swami Dayananda Saraswati located the original home of the Aryans in:
ndd73861c963.x: Dayananda Saraswati (Satyarth Prakash) placed the homeland in Tibet; Penka chose Germany and P. Giles Hungary and the Danube valley.

nc1d864e8ccc.s: Who linked Painted Grey Ware with the Vedic tradition?
nc1d864e8ccc.x: B. B. Lal identified the Sarasvati with the Rigvedic river and linked Painted Grey Ware with the Vedic tradition.

nf2c028951a9.s: The Harappans are described as using:
nf2c028951a9.x: Harappans used solid wheels, while spoked-wheel chariots form part of the migration argument.

nccaebeafaf9.s: In the Aryan debate, the Andronovo culture represents:
o: Steppe pastoralists with horses and chariots
A Harappan port with a dockyard
nccaebeafaf9.x: Andronovo is associated with steppe pastoralists, horses and chariots, linked to Indo-Iranian speakers.

n8efada0cec3.s: Who popularised the concept of 'Aryan' in modern scholarship?
n8efada0cec3.x: Max Muller popularised the concept; 'Aryan' denotes a linguistic-cultural group, not a superior race.

ne0caf4b184d.s: The link between Painted Grey Ware and Later Vedic textual geography is:
ne0caf4b184d.x: The relationship between Painted Grey Ware archaeology and Later Vedic geography remains an open question.

n4d056a0a937.s: Which tribe emerged dominant after the Battle of Ten Kings?
n4d056a0a937.x: The Bharatas emerged dominant; the defeated Purus later allied with them to form the Kurus.

nd6109bca762.s: The Early Vedic geographical core lay in:
nd6109bca762.x: The Early Vedic core was Punjab–Haryana; the Later Vedic core shifted east to the Doab, eastern UP and Bihar.

o: A Hindu Kush mountain associated with Soma
n4792797172a.x: Mujavant is a Hindu Kush mountain associated with Soma; Himavant is the Himalayas and Dhanva desert land.

n18c9ff757c7.s: Which river is mentioned most often in the Rigveda?
n18c9ff757c7.x: The Sindhu is the most mentioned river; the Yamuna is mentioned thrice and the Ganga once.

n229cb967aa7.s: In the Battle of Ten Kings, Sudas was supported by the priest:
n229cb967aa7.x: Sudas, Bharata chief of the Tritsu family, was supported by Vasishtha, not Vishvamitra; the battle is in Mandala VII.

n4f28dac32de.s: The Rigvedic river Kubha is identified with the:
n4f28dac32de.x: Kubha is the Kabul; Krumu is the Kurram, Gomati the Gomal and Suvastu the Swat, showing links with Afghanistan.

nf8930995c2b.s: The Battle of Ten Kings is traditionally traced to the rivalry between:
nf8930995c2b.x: Tradition traces the battle to the Vasishtha-Vishvamitra rivalry; the Rigveda is religious poetry, not a chronicle.

nindian-history-16-4.s: In Vedic geography, 'Madhya Desh' was the region between the:
nindian-history-16-4.x: Madhya Desh lay between the Himalayas and the Vindhyas; Aryavarta was northern India occupied by the Aryans.

n3882a75350a.s: Which of the following was NOT among the Panchajana of the Rigvedic period?
n3882a75350a.x: The Panchajana were Yadus, Turvasas, Anus, Druhyus and Purus; the Kikatas of south Bihar were outside it.

n255f5b093f1.s: Which assembly is mentioned most often in the Rigveda?
n255f5b093f1.x: Vidatha is mentioned 122 times, against 9 for the Samiti and 8 for the Sabha.

n6a0aecad305.x: Divodasa, the Bharata chief, defeated Sambara.

n9080223d028.s: The Rigvedic Rajan was known by the title:
n9080223d028.x: The Rajan was called Gopati or Gopajanasya, protector of the tribe and its cattle.

nb9f98b49688.s: Women members of the Vedic Sabha were called:
nb9f98b49688.x: Women attended the Sabha and Vidatha, and female Sabha members were called Sabhavati.

naffcedd88a9.s: The Ratnins are associated with which period?
naffcedd88a9.x: Ratnins, hereditary territorial kingship, regular taxes and royal sacrifices belong to the Later Vedic period.

nfffec6ee3f2.s: In the early Vedic polity, the 'Spasa' was a:
nfffec6ee3f2.x: Spasa was the spy; Senani the army commander, Purohita the chief priest and Vrajapati the pasture officer.

ndd12c7521e3.x: The Sena was a temporary militia; there was no standing army and no regular tax machinery.

n60ae09aa544.s: The Rigvedic river Drishadvati is identified with the:
n60ae09aa544.x: Drishadvati is the Chautang; Sarasvati is the Ghaggar-Hakra, Vipas the Beas and Sutudri the Sutlej.

n0f5956e1262.s: Which river was called 'Naditama' in the Rigveda?
n0f5956e1262.x: The Sarasvati was the most sacred river, called Naditama; the Sindhu was the most mentioned.

n2b06e08afe0.s: The Rigvedic river Parushni is the modern:
n2b06e08afe0.x: Parushni is the Ravi; Vitasta is the Jhelum and Asikni the Chenab.

n41c594a2e77.s: Early Vedic weapons were made of:
n41c594a2e77.x: Early Vedic weapons were of bronze, not iron; horse-drawn chariots, coats of mail and helmets were used.

n784d3a9977d.s: The first reference to the word 'Andhra' occurs in the story of:
n784d3a9977d.x: 'Andhra' first appears in the Aitareya Brahmana in the Sunahshepa story, not in the Rig Veda.

nindian-history-16-14.x: Devitama means best of goddesses; Matetama is best of mothers and Naditama best of rivers.

nb40eb1b31a8.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven rivers of the Sapta Sindhu?
nb40eb1b31a8.x: The Sapta Sindhu are Sindhu, Vitasta, Asikni, Parushni, Vipas, Sutudri and Sarasvati.

n7c1449b8577.x: Samudra means a collection or body of water and does not necessarily denote the sea.

n78477805c69.s: In the Vedic period, the head of the family was called:
n78477805c69.x: The family head was the Kulapa or Kulapati; Vrajapati was the pasture officer and Ugra a police official.
